content: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children, commonly referred to as WIC, is a federally funded assistance program administered by the Food and Nutrition Service (FNS) of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). This program is specifically designed to provide healthcare and nutritional support to low-income pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, and children under the age of five. Eligibility for WIC is automatically granted to individuals who participate in other benefit programs, such as the Food Stamp Program, Medicaid, or Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), or if their family members are participants in these programs. It is important to note that WIC is distinct and separate from the USDA's Food Stamp Program. The WIC program was established through legislation introduced in 1972 by Senator Hubert Humphrey of Minnesota and was made a permanent program in 1975. Participants in the WIC program often receive monthly checks or vouchers that can be used to purchase specific food items. In economically disadvantaged areas, specialized WIC stores have historically existed, which exclusively sell food items that can be purchased using WIC vouchers issued by the state program. These stores do not accept any other forms of payment. WIC stores have been known to charge the maximum allowable price under the program, which can be up to 16% higher than the prices for the same food items in regular retail stores. In 2006, the federal government implemented cost-cutting measures, which included a ruling aimed at phasing out WIC stores. This decision led to significant changes in the program's structure. The WIC store association filed a class-action lawsuit in response to these measures but ultimately lost the case. Over the past two years, more than 80% of WIC stores have closed due to the government's cost-cutting initiatives. These measures required WIC stores to sell products at prices below cost, which, for over 90% of items, were even lower than the prices at major retailers such as Walmart and similar stores.
